items.title: Neural variability reliably encodes interindividual differences in the perception of pain intensity
items.authors: Zhang et al.
items.feature_family: Temporal response variance / standard deviation
items.feature_definition: Temporal SD of EEG responses; primary variability measure in 100-ms sliding windows, compared with evoked-response amplitude.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: response variability can add information about between-person differences in pain-intensity discriminability beyond mean evoked amplitude.
items.verified_result_metric: Authors report robust, replicated correlations with pain-intensity discriminability across six EEG datasets (N=633); no numeric coefficient copied here.
items.prediction_target: Between-person pain intensity discriminability (difference in mean ratings for low vs high stimuli).
items.validation_design: Association replicated across several EEG datasets; multiple sensory modalities and patient/healthy cohorts; not a prospectively held-out clinical prediction model.
items.data_evidence: Article states data and code are on OSF; repository content could not be independently inspected, so raw-vs-derived EEG availability is not verified.
items.relevance_limitations: Directly relevant variance evidence, but per-stimulus 100-ms variability and inter-individual discrimination differ from 5-s resting-window features; source interpretation is association, not a validated predictor. No use of spectral feature interpretation.

items.title: Selective and replicable neuroimaging-based indicators of pain discriminability
items.authors: Zhang et al.
items.feature_family: Evoked-potential response amplitude and latency; pain AUC
items.feature_definition: Differences in N2/P2 peak amplitude and latency; signal-detection-theory AUC operationalizes an individual’s pain discriminability.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: evoked EEG response features may estimate how sensitively an individual distinguishes pain intensity, not moment-to-moment pain itself.
items.verified_result_metric: LASSO-predicted AUC correlated with measured pain AUC: Pearson r=0.536 in Dataset 1 and r=0.423 in Dataset 2 (both p<0.0001). These are correlations, not R²/accuracy.
items.prediction_target: Individual pain-intensity discriminability (AUC).
items.validation_design: Three EEG cohorts (N=114,111,141); exploratory Dataset 1 and replication in Datasets 2/3; pain-selectivity assessed against non-pain sensory modalities.
items.data_evidence: Linked EEG dataset paper lists raw BIDS records including ds005292; this specific data page describes trialwise pain ratings.
items.relevance_limitations: Peak-based, stimulus-locked feature design requires event-aligned epochs and broad scalp electrodes; article’s AUC target is not a pain rating forecast and its evidence is not based on 5-s resting windows.

items.title: External validation of binary machine learning models for pain intensity perception classification from EEG in healthy individuals
items.authors: Mari et al.
items.feature_family: Single-trial time-frequency EEG features
items.feature_definition: Peri-stimulus, single-trial time-frequency features over selected frontal, central and parietal electrodes.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: independent-sample validation tests whether pain-intensity patterns generalize beyond the training cohort and stimulation protocol.
items.verified_result_metric: Random Forest accuracy: 73.18% cross-validation, 68.32% external validation with identical stimulation, 60.42% external validation with changed stimulation. Accuracy only; no variance-explained claim.
items.prediction_target: Low versus high experimental pain intensity.
items.validation_design: Study 1 n=25 training/cross-validation; study 2 n=15 external validation, with a second changed stimulation protocol.
items.data_evidence: Paper describes two experimental datasets but no publicly accessible raw EEG repository was verified in its Data Availability statement in the captured article.
items.relevance_limitations: Event-locked features and frontal/parietal channels; not directly reproduced by C3/C4/Cz-only, 1–40-Hz, 5-s windows. Cross-validation and external performance differ materially.

items.title: An Innovative EEG-Based Pain Identification and Quantification: A Pilot Study
items.authors: Segning et al.
items.feature_family: Envelope coefficient of variation / signal-strength variability
items.feature_definition: Average coefficient of variation of the Hilbert-derived upper envelope in beta (13–30 Hz), termed Piqβ; recordings at rest and repeated pain report every 30 s.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors propose beta-envelope variability as an objective pain-presence/magnitude indicator; inference: windowed amplitude dispersion is a plausible pain-related signal-strength feature.
items.verified_result_metric: Authors report proposed Piqβ threshold ≥10% for pain presence and qualitatively higher Piqβ with greater pain; no verified accuracy, correlation coefficient, R² or external validation.
items.prediction_target: Pain presence and magnitude / self-reported pain intensity.
items.validation_design: Pilot groups: 7 healthy with pain, 15 experimentally induced thermal pain, 66 chronic-pain participants; repeated ratings; threshold proposed from study, no independent validation stated.
items.data_evidence: Captured article provides participant/method/result information but no verified public raw EEG repository link.
items.relevance_limitations: Uses contralateral motor electrodes and beta-band envelope, not a validated generic variance predictor; 30-s ratings/window timing do not align to a 5-s model; only 13–30 Hz overlaps pipeline passband.

items.title: Towards the Objective Identification of the Presence of Pain Based on Electroencephalography Signals’ Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept
items.authors: Segning et al.
items.feature_family: Envelope coefficient of variation across EEG bands
items.feature_definition: Coefficient of variation of Hilbert upper envelope (CVUE) from FC5 and T7 in alpha, beta and gamma bands.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors proposed higher CVUEβ as a candidate indicator of pain presence; inference: variability in envelope amplitude may complement absolute signal amplitude.
items.verified_result_metric: Authors report CVUEβ rose up to 20% in pain at rest, but found no correlation with pain intensity or task performance; no classification accuracy or predictive R² verified.
items.prediction_target: Pain presence (group/condition); pain intensity examined as a separate correlate.
items.validation_design: Proof-of-concept: 4 chronic fibromyalgia participants and 7 healthy volunteers exposed to capsaicin; baseline and active/task conditions, small sample.
items.data_evidence: No public raw EEG dataset link verified in captured article.
items.relevance_limitations: FC5/T7 are frontal-temporal channels absent from pipeline; gamma upper edge 43 Hz partly excluded by 40-Hz filter; condition/timing and small N limit transfer. The source explicitly reports no CVUEβ–pain-intensity correlation.

items.title: A systematic review of neurophysiological sensing for the assessment of acute pain
items.authors: Fernandez Rojas et al.
items.feature_family: Review of EEG response strength/variability and prediction designs
items.feature_definition: Synthesizes acute-pain neurophysiological sensing, EEG feature engineering, and classification/regression studies from 2013–July 2022.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: useful as a map of candidate labels, feature definitions and study designs; does not itself validate a signal-strength feature.
items.verified_result_metric: Review included 48 studies overall; no single pooled EEG variance/SNR effect or pooled prediction metric verified.
items.prediction_target: Acute pain assessment across reviewed studies.
items.validation_design: Systematic literature review; search July 2022; review-level evidence, not an independent validation cohort.
items.data_evidence: Review article; no new raw EEG data.
items.relevance_limitations: Broad sensing review includes non-EEG modalities and feature-focused studies; use only EEG-specific entries and do not treat review totals as EEG-only.

items.title: Denoising EEG Signals for Real-World BCI Applications Using GANs
items.authors: Brophy et al.
items.feature_family: Denoising quality: SNR, RRMSE, correlation and band power
items.feature_definition: GAN reconstructs cleaned EEG; denoising evaluated using SNR, relative RMSE, Pearson correlation and frequency-band power ratios.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: compare denoising before/after downstream analysis; signal cleanup cannot be presumed to improve task prediction.
items.verified_result_metric: For one reported classifier, ground-truth accuracy/F1 were 88.75%/0.8987 and denoised-data accuracy/F1 were 77.94%/0.7799; downstream accuracy decreased after denoising.
items.prediction_target: Artifact-free EEG reconstruction and downstream BCI classification (not pain).
items.validation_design: Authors evaluated multiple artifact types; supplied dataset/task evaluations, but no pain cohorts.
items.data_evidence: Article says original contributions are in article/supplementary material; further inquiries directed to corresponding author. This does not verify public raw EEG access.
items.relevance_limitations: General EEG denoising method, transferable only; BCI task is not pain and reported post-denoising classifier decrement cautions against equating SNR improvement with better pain prediction.

items.title: Embedding decomposition for artifacts removal in EEG signals (DeepSeparator)
items.authors: Yu et al.
items.feature_family: Denoising reconstruction error / correlation / signal quality
items.feature_definition: Embedding-space separation of EEG and artifact; evaluates temporal and spectral relative RMSE and correlation against clean reference, across simulated EOG/EMG noise.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: clean reference benchmarks can test whether variance or signal-strength features are preserved after denoising.
items.verified_result_metric: On semi-synthetic test data authors report lower temporal/spectral RRMSE and higher correlation than comparison methods; no numeric effect transcribed.
items.prediction_target: Artifact removal / signal reconstruction, not pain.
items.validation_design: Held-out 10,000 semi-synthetic test segments plus real task EEG evaluation; code and benchmark referenced.
items.data_evidence: Article uses EEGdenoiseNet semi-synthetic data; repository links the public dataset; DeepSeparator source repository is also public.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable method only. Semi-synthetic EEG quality scores are not pain prediction metrics; benchmark sample segmentation/SNR differs from pain event baseline design.

items.title: EEGdenoiseNet: a benchmark dataset for deep learning solutions of EEG denoising
items.authors: Zhang et al.
items.feature_family: Known-SNR artifact mixtures; temporal/spectral RRMSE and correlation
items.feature_definition: 4514 clean EEG segments, 3400 EOG and 5598 EMG segments enable controlled mixtures with clean reference and varied SNR.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: controlled amplitude/noise perturbations support testing robustness of variance and strength features to artifact burden.
items.verified_result_metric: Authors benchmarked four networks with temporal/spectral RRMSE and correlation under controlled contamination; no pain result and no specific model metric quoted.
items.prediction_target: Denoising/reconstruction (not pain).
items.validation_design: Benchmark comparisons on semi-synthetic mixtures with known clean targets; public data and code.
items.data_evidence: Paper states structured dataset publicly available; repo contains 4514 clean EEG, 3400 ocular artifact and 5598 muscle artifact epochs; G-node link provides additional 512-Hz EEG/EMG.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable denoising benchmark, not pain-labelled; synthetic SNR mixtures do not establish pain-related signal strength.

items.title: AnEEG: leveraging deep learning for effective artifact removal in EEG data
items.authors: Kalita et al.
items.feature_family: NMSE, RMSE, correlation coefficient, SNR and signal-to-artifact ratio
items.feature_definition: LSTM/GAN artifact-removal system evaluated on reconstructed signals with NMSE, RMSE, CC, SNR and SAR.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: a preprocessing robustness benchmark could compare pain-relevant feature stability before and after denoising.
items.verified_result_metric: Authors report lower NMSE/RMSE and higher CC/SNR/SAR than wavelet-decomposition baselines; no independent pain metric and no exact value quoted.
items.prediction_target: EEG artifact removal/reconstruction, not pain.
items.validation_design: Authors describe five participants’ 32-channel 128-Hz recordings and a subject-held-out split; semi-synthetic/benchmark comparisons also described.
items.data_evidence: Article reports its own small data collection but no verified public raw EEG repository link was saved; cited datasets in background are not the study’s dataset.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable only. Its 128-Hz, 0.5–40-Hz, 5-s segmentation is unusually close to the stated pipeline, but it uses 32 channels and artifact tasks, not pain labels; wavelet targets may bias reference truth.

items.title: A comprehensive EEG dataset of laser-evoked potentials for pain research
items.authors: Zhao et al.
items.feature_family: Raw EEG signal strength/variance; trialwise pain reports
items.feature_definition: Dataset paper describes 678 healthy participants’ high-density EEG, nine experiments, variable laser intensities, and single-trial NRS labels; preprocessing includes 1–100 Hz and 3-s event windows.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: large raw trial-level data supports prospective analyses of signal variance versus repeated pain ratings and preprocessing robustness.
items.verified_result_metric: Dataset descriptor only; no new prediction score or variance-explained result claimed by the paper.
items.prediction_target: Single-trial pain rating and pain discriminability; not a trained predictor in the data descriptor.
items.validation_design: Nine source experiments (N=26,29,39,30,65,95,142,223,29); paper records raw BIDS and preprocessing derivatives, no held-out prediction evaluation.
items.data_evidence: Paper states raw BIDS EEG is publicly shared, links nine OpenNeuro accessions; single-trial NRS after laser stimuli, and derivatives documented.
items.relevance_limitations: High density / 1000–1024-Hz systems and 3-s (-1 to +2 s) baseline-corrected epochs differ from C3/C4/Cz, 128 Hz and 5-s windows; trials/ratings and recording system differ across cohorts.

items.title: EEGdenoiseNet
items.authors: Zhang et al.; dataset repository by NCCLab
items.feature_family: Known-clean EEG and EOG/EMG artifact reference segments
items.feature_definition: Public benchmark dataset contains clean EEG and separate ocular/muscle artifact segments for controlled synthetic contamination.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: use as transferable artifact/SNR stress-test only, never as evidence about pain-associated EEG.
items.verified_result_metric: Not applicable; resource, no pain prediction result.
items.prediction_target: No pain target; benchmark data enables denoising method evaluation.
items.validation_design: Dataset resource; benchmark paper evaluates models, repository provides downloadable data/code.
items.open_access_status: Publicly accessible repository; dataset README and downloadable data links observed.
items.data_evidence: Repository README enumerates clean EEG/EOG/EMG segment counts and links supplementary 512-Hz segments at G-node; paper identifies the repository.
items.relevance_limitations: Not pain-labeled; semi-synthetic contamination should only test artifact sensitivity, not provide pain training/validation.

items.title: DeepSeparator reference implementation
items.authors: NCCLab contributors; linked to Yu et al.
items.feature_family: Denoising/embedding decomposition implementation
items.feature_definition: Open code implements encoder/decomposer/decoder EEG artifact separation and denoising; training and prediction scripts documented.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: reproducibility can support an artifact-robustness sensitivity analysis before pain feature modeling.
items.verified_result_metric: Not applicable; software resource.
items.prediction_target: No pain target; applies to artifacted EEG.
items.validation_design: Public repository provides code, setup notes and EEGdenoiseNet data instructions.
items.data_evidence: Repository names the EEGdenoiseNet benchmark and links to data plus G-node supplements.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable EEG tool, not pain-specific; legacy dependencies and semi-synthetic ground-truth assumptions require review.

items.title: EEGdenoiseNet benchmark code
items.authors: NCCLab contributors; linked to Zhang et al.
items.feature_family: Denoising benchmarks / metrics
items.feature_definition: Repository supplies code and scripts for EEGdenoiseNet benchmark networks and controlled noise mixtures.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: a reproducible reference may support fixed-SNR stress testing for feature robustness.
items.verified_result_metric: Not applicable; software resource.
items.prediction_target: No pain target; EEG denoising benchmark.
items.validation_design: Repository separates code and data; paper reports four benchmark networks.
items.data_evidence: Repository lists `code` and `data` folders and data counts; paper links same repo.
items.relevance_limitations: No pain labels; results are not transferred pain-prediction evidence.

conflicts: Variability is not synonymous with variance explained: the large pain-variability study measures temporal SD and reports association with interindividual pain discriminability; it does not establish that an arbitrary window-variance feature explains pain ratings or yields a cross-validated R².

Metric types are incommensurate: Mari et al. report classification accuracy; Zhang et al. report Pearson correlations between predicted and observed AUC; none should be relabelled as variance explained. Piqβ/CVUE threshold findings are not accuracy/R² claims.

The 678-person raw dataset uses 1000/1024-Hz acquisition and stimulus-aligned 3-s epochs with pre-stimulus baseline; ds005286/ds005291 README pages report 100-ms laser marker delay. Existing 128-Hz five-second C3/C4/Cz processing cannot assume those timing conventions transfer unchanged.

C3/C4/Cz, 1–40-Hz pipeline excludes frontal channels used by some pain-presence results and removes all >40-Hz content; high-gamma 60–85 Hz is above the 64-Hz Nyquist frequency at 128 Hz and cannot be recovered. CVUE pilot beta 13–30 Hz overlaps but uses contralateral motor electrodes and 30-s ratings.

Denoising improvements on signal metrics do not imply better downstream prediction: the GAN paper reports lower classifier accuracy/F1 after denoising than on ground truth in its example. Denoising should be validated against preserved physiological feature and task validity, not SNR alone.
gaps: No verified public raw EEG repository was confirmed for the two small CVUE/Piqβ signal-strength pilot studies or Mari et al. external-validation cohort; included numeric results are not a substitute for accessible raw data.
OSF QTV8A is cited by the 2025 PLOS variability article for data and code, but repository contents were not independently opened; raw EEG vs processed/derived measures remain unverified.

No source in this area establishes a validated pain predictor based only on 5-s C3/C4/Cz windows after 1–40-Hz filtering. Existing task labels are often event-locked, sub-second or rated every 15–30 s.

A systematic search did not establish a direct EEG-to-pain R² / variance-explained benchmark with public raw EEG and truly external validation. Do not infer R² from r, accuracy, SNR or classification results.

Dataset collection component accessions vary in amplifier, montage, stimulation/ratings, marker delay and preprocessed derivatives; assess provenance, event metadata, and overlap before combining. Component dataset descriptors are resources, not separate papers.
